utriculate: Resembling a bladder; swollen like a bladder; inflated; utricular. Dana.
utility: 1. The quality or state of being useful; usefulness; production of good; profitableness to some valuable end; as, the utility of manure upon land; the utility of the sciences; the utility of medicines. The utility of the enterprises was, however, so great and obvious that all opposition proved useless. Macaulay. 2. (Polit. Econ.) Adaptation to satisfy the desires or wants;
utopia: 1. An imaginary island, represented by Sir Thomas More, in a work called Utopia, as enjoying the greatest perfection in politics, laws, and the like. See Utopia, in the Dictionary of Noted Names in Fiction. 2. Hence, any place or state of ideal perfection.
uterus: 1. (Anat.) The organ of a female mammal in which the young are developed previous to birth; the womb. Note: The uterus is simply an enlargement of the oviduct, and in the lower mammals there is one on each side, but in the higher forms the two become more or less completely united into one.
utilitarian: 1. Of or pertaining to utility; consisting in utility; as, utilitarian narrowness; a utilitarian indifference to art. 2. Of or pertaining to utilitarianism; supporting utilitarianism; | One who holds the doctrine of utilitarianism. The utilitarians are for merging all the particular virtues into one, and would substitute in their place the greatest usefulness, as the alone principle…
utro: - (connection with, or relation to, the uterus; as in utro- ovarian.
utilization: The act of utilizing, or the state of being utilized.
utricularia: A genus of aquatic flowering plants, in which the submersed leaves bear many little utricles, or ascidia. See Ascidium,
utricle: 1. A little sac or vesicle, as the air cell of fucus, or seaweed. 2. (Physiol.) A microscopic cell in the structure of an egg, animal, or plant. 3. (Bot.) A small, thin-walled, one-seeded fruit, as of goosefoot. Gray. 4. (Anat.) A utriculus.
utero: - (connection with, or relation to, the uterus; as in utro- ovarian.
utilize: To make useful; to turn to profitable account or use; to make use of; as, to utilize the whole power of a machine; to utilize one's opportunities. In former ages, the mile-long corridors, with their numerous alcoves, might have been utilized as . . . dungeons. Hawthorne.
utopianism: The ideas, views, aims, etc., of a Utopian; impracticable schemes of human perfection; optimism.
utterest: Uttermost. To the utterest proof of her courage. Chaucer.
utricular: 1. Of or pertaining to a utricle, or utriculus; containing, or furnished with, a utricle or utricles; utriculate; as, a utricular plant. 2. Resembling a utricle or bag, whether large or minute;
utterless: Incapable of being uttered. (old) A clamoring debate of utterless things. Milton.
uterogestation: Gestation in the womb from conception to birth; pregnancy. Pritchard.
utica: Of, pertaining to, or designating, a subdivision of the Trenton Period of the Lower Silurian, characterized in the State of New York by beds of shale.
uttermost: Extreme; utmost; being; in the farthest, greatest, or highest degree; as, the uttermost extent or end. "In this uttermost distress." Milton. | The utmost; the highest or greatest degree; the farthest extent. Tennyson. Wherefore he is able also to save them to the uttermost that come unto God by him. Heb. vii. 25.
utmost: 1. Situated at the farthest point or extremity; farthest out; most distant; extreme; as, the utmost limits of the land; the utmost extent of human knowledge. Spenser. | The most that can be; the farthest limit; the greatest power, degree, or effort; as, he has done his utmost; try your utmost. We have tried the utmost of our friends. Shak.
utia: Any species of large West Indian rodents of the genus Capromys, or Utia. In general appearance and habits they resemble rats, but they are as large as rabbits.
utter: 1. Outer. "Thine utter eyen." Chaucer. (old) "By him a shirt and utter mantle laid." Chapman. As doth an hidden moth The inner garment fret, not th' utter touch. Spenser. 2. | 1. To put forth or out; to reach out. (old) How bragly [proudly] it begins to bud, And utter his tender head. Spenser. 2. To dispose of in trade; to sell or vend.
utilizable: Capable of being utilized; as, the utilizable products of the gas works.
utipossidetis: 1. (Internat. Law) The basis or principle of a treaty which leaves belligerents mutually in possession of what they have acquired by their arms during the war. Brande & C. 2. (Roman Law) A species of interdict granted to one who was in possession of an immovable thing, in order that he might be declared the legal possessor. Burrill.
utopian: Of or pertaining to Utopia; resembling Utopia; hence, ideal; chimerical; fanciful; founded upon, or involving, imaginary perfections; as, Utopian projects; Utopian happiness. | An inhabitant of Utopia; hence, one who believes in the perfectibility of human society; a visionary; an idealist; an optimist. Hooker.
utas: 1. (O. Eng. Law) The eighth day after any term or feast; the octave; as, the utas of St. Michael. Cowell. The marriage was celebrated and Canterbury, and in the utas of St. Hilary next ensuing she was crowned. Holinshed. 2. Hence, festivity; merriment. (old) Shak.
utterly: In an utter manner; to the full extent; fully; totally; as, utterly ruined; it is utterly vain.
utraquist: One who receives the eucharist in both kinds; esp., one of a body of Hussites who in the 15th century fought for the right to do this. Called also Calixtines.
utensil: That which is used; an instrument; an implement; especially, an instrument or vessel used in a kitchen, or in domestic and farming business. Wagons fraught with utensils of war. Milton.
utterance: 1. The act of uttering. Specifically: -- (a) Sale by offering to the public. (old) Bacon. (b) Putting in circulation; as, the utterance of false coin, or of forged notes. (c) Vocal expression; | The last extremity; the end; death; outrance. (old) Annibal forced those captives whom he had taken of our men to skirmish one against another to the utterance. Holland.
utriculoid: Resembling a bladder; utricular; utriculate. Dana.
uterine: 1. Of or instrument to the uterus, or womb. 2. Born of the same mother, but by a different father. Walter Pope, uterine brother to Dr. Joh. WilkiWood.
utriculus: A little sac, or bag; a utricle; especially, a part of the membranous labyrinth of the ear. See the Note under Ear.
utes: An extensive tribe of North American Indians of the Shoshone stock, inhabiting Colorado, Utah, New Mexico, Arizona, and adjacent regions. They are subdivided into several subordinate tribes, some of which are among the most degraded of North American Indians.
utterness: The quality or state of being utter, or extreme; extremity; utmost; uttermost.
utilitarianism: 1. The doctrine that the greatest happiness of the greatest number should be the end and aim of all social and political institutions. Bentham. 2. The doctrine that virtue is founded in utility, or that virtue is defined and enforced by its tendency to promote the highest happiness of the universe. J. S. Mill. 3.
ut: The first note in Guido's musical scale, now usually superseded by do. See Solmization.
uterovaginal: Pertaining to both the uterus and the vagina.
